newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Aid workers say Tutsis take second east Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers say Tutsis take second east Zaire town.

text.p: Ethnic Zairean Tutsis fighting Zairean troops were reported to have seized a town north of east Zaire's Goma region near vast camps housing 700,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees next to Rwanda's border, aid workers said on Saturday.

Aid workers currently in Geneva, citing field reports, said they feared large numbers of refugees could flee their camps in Goma after Tutsi Banyamulenge fighters who are resisting Zairean attempts to force them back to Rwanda captured Rutshuru town on Friday. Rutshuru is some 10 km (six miles) from the Hutu camps.

Earlier, a U.N. official in the region said thousands of Rwandan Hutus fled the sprawling camp of Kibumba, home to 190,000 Rwandan Hutus and next to Rwanda's mountainous border, in Goma on Saturday because of fighting, a U.N. aid official.
Reports from aid workers described Rutshuru as "a war zone".
The fighters are drawn from ethnic Banyamulenge Tutsis who came to Zaire as long ago as the end of the 18th century.

Many among the Rwandan refugees killed or watched others kill during 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis. Hutu militia in camps in Goma stage frequent raids into Rwanda. Aid workers expect the Tutsi guerrillas to try to empty the camps and force the Hutus away from Rwanda's borders.
